title: ⚡ Conditionals

sections.heading: The four types
sections.body:
Type 0 (always true): If + present, present
"If you heat ice, it melts."

Type 1 (real future): If + present, will + infinitive
"If emissions rise, temperatures will increase."

Type 2 (hypothetical present): If + past simple, would + infinitive
"If governments invested more, outcomes would improve."

Type 3 (hypothetical past): If + past perfect, would have + past participle
"If action had been taken sooner, the crisis could have been avoided."

sections.heading: Mixed conditionals (Band 8+)
sections.body:
Mixed conditionals combine time frames:

Past condition → present result:
"If she had studied medicine (past), she would be a doctor now (present)."

Present condition → past result:
"If he were more careful (present), he would not have made that error (past)."

highlight: Type 2 and Type 3 are most common in IELTS essays. Using Type 3 correctly signals Band 8+ grammatical range.

example.wrong: If governments will invest in renewables, emissions reduce.
example.right: If governments were to invest substantially in renewables, carbon emissions would fall dramatically within a decade.

question: Which is a correct Type 1 (First) conditional?
options: If temperatures rise, sea levels will increase.
If temperatures rose, sea levels would increase.
If temperatures will rise, sea levels increase.
If temperatures had risen, sea levels would have increased.
correct: If temperatures rise, sea levels will increase.
explanation:
Type 1: If + PRESENT SIMPLE, will + INFINITIVE

Type 2 would be: "If temperatures ROSE, sea levels WOULD increase"
Type 3 would be: "If temperatures HAD RISEN, sea levels WOULD HAVE increased"

Never use "will" in the if-clause of a conditional.
hint: Type 1 = real future possibility. Structure: if + present, will + base verb.

question: Choose the correct Type 2 (Second) conditional:
options: If the government invests in education, literacy rates would improve.
If the government invested in education, literacy rates would improve.
If the government had invested in education, literacy rates improve.
If the government will invest in education, literacy rates would improve.
correct: If the government invested in education, literacy rates would improve.
explanation:
Type 2: If + PAST SIMPLE (invested), WOULD + infinitive (improve)

This expresses a hypothetical or unlikely scenario in the present/future.

❌ "invests" with "would" mixes Type 1 and Type 2
❌ "had invested" is Type 3 (past hypothetical)
❌ Never "will" in the if-clause
hint: Type 2: if + past simple... would + bare infinitive. Hypothetical present/future.

sentence: If the industrial revolution _______ occurred earlier, modern technology _______ developed far more rapidly.
explanation:
Type 3 conditional: IF + past perfect (had occurred) + WOULD HAVE + past participle (developed)

Both blanks are crucial:
• "had occurred" = past perfect in the if-clause
• "would have developed" = modal perfect in the result clause
hint: Type 3: If + had + past participle... would have + past participle.

question: "_____ the government to act decisively, the crisis could have been averted." Which opening is correct?
explanation:
"Had the government acted decisively" = formal Type 3 conditional INVERSION.

When we remove "if" and invert, Type 3 uses HAD:
"If the government had acted" → "Had the government acted"

Type 2 inversion uses WERE: "Were I in charge..."
Modal inversion uses SHOULD: "Should you need help..."

This is a Band 9 structure — examiners reward it highly.
hint: Type 3 inversion: remove "if", put HAD first, then subject.
